clusters.headline_hint: Powerful nor'easter batters US Northeast, causing severe flooding, travel disruption, and widespread blackout

claims.text: A powerful nor'easter storm brought flooding and power outages across the northeastern United States on Saturday.
More than 400 flights were cancelled and power outages affected over 88,000 homes and businesses as of Saturday afternoon.
The governors of New York and New Jersey declared states of emergency in counties expected to be worst hit by the storm, including New York City.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul said, "Anyone who goes in or near the water this weekend is literally gambling with their life."
Musician Ed Sheeran's scheduled concerts in Massachusetts on Friday and Saturday were cancelled due to the storm.
New York officials warned of wind gusts reaching up to 55 mph (86 km/h) throughout the weekend.
The Boston Red Sox rescheduled the last game of their series against the Chicago Cubs to Sunday afternoon in Florida.
A professional football match between Red Bull New York and St Louis City SC was cancelled due to the weather.
US Weather Prediction Center senior forecaster Bob Oravec stated storm surges were expected to raise ocean levels by three feet along the New Jersey and New York coasts.
Poweroutage.com reported that 101,674 homes and businesses from Massachusetts to Maryland were without power as of 1:15 p.m. Saturday.
The estimated rainfall forecast for New York City doubled to six inches on Saturday, causing power outages for about 22,000 customers.
The Long Island Rail Road suspended service on its Long Beach Branch due to flooding on Saturday.
Kenny Formica, a marina owner in Surf City, New Jersey, reported that a customer's 25ft boat worth $150,000 blew off its lift during the storm.
Sea Bright Mayor Brian Kelly said he expected street flooding in his town to reach up to 6ft, comparing it to an "Irene-scale flooding event".
Officials in Manasquan, New Jersey, issued a voluntary evacuation for residents in low-lying areas.

clusters.headline_hint: Trump rejects Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days

claims.text: US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping within seven days.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Tehran would wait for the "definitive views" of mediators regarding Trump's comments before making a decision.
The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed to shipping since war broke out between the US, Israel, and Iran in late February.
Yemen's Houthis seized strategic stretches of Yemen's Red Sea coast, including the port of Mokha overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi proposed a seven-day plan requiring the US to lift its naval blockade, waive oil sanctions, and agree to a ceasefire covering Lebanon in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated to Fox News that Iran had signed an agreement based on the June memorandum of understanding and remained willing to move forward.
US President Donald Trump posted an image on Truth Social showing the Strait of Hormuz labelled as "Trump Strait".
Under a memorandum of understanding signed in June, Iran promised not to seek a nuclear weapon and to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in return for U.S. naval blockade relief and eased sanctions.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told CBS that Iran would permit UN nuclear inspectors to enter the country if the US accepts its proposal to reopen the strait and resume nuclear negotiations.
US President Donald Trump has rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to shipping.
The Wall Street Journal reported that US President Donald Trump told aides he expects to resume a bombing campaign against Iran after the US midterm elections in November.
Saudi Arabia expressed concern that Iran's proposed Hormuz route deal was a bilateral agreement between Iran and Oman rather than involving Gulf states as joint signatories.

clusters.headline_hint: US and China agree to high-level AI dialogue and selective tariff relief following Trump-Xi meeting

claims.text: The United States and China agreed to reduce tariffs on $30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction following President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington.
The agreed tariff reductions cover US exports such as agricultural goods, wood, and cosmetics, and US imports including small appliances, toys, and decorations.
US President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House that the US should not integrate AI initiatives with China because the US is leading China by a lot.
US President Donald Trump stated upon departing the White House that the US is not going to put brakes on artificial intelligence development.
The White House stated on Friday that the US and China agreed to establish a bilateral communication channel for artificial intelligence incidents.
US President Donald Trump announced that his administration would rename artificial intelligence as "super intelligence" or SI in official communications.
China's Foreign Ministry stated that Beijing respects Washington's position and switch in phrasing from artificial intelligence to "super intelligence".
Chinese Vice President Han Zheng indirectly asked the US to respect the sovereignty of Iran and Cuba during his speech at the UN General Assembly.
US President Donald Trump had previously warned Chinese President Xi Jinping against supplying shoulder-mounted air-defence missile launchers to Iran and helping Iran evade oil sanctions.
The US and China agreed to extend their trade truce by two months beyond its scheduled November 10 expiration date.
Chinese President Xi Jinping concluded a three-day summit visit to Washington with US President Donald Trump on Friday.

clusters.headline_hint: Russia and Ukraine trade lethal air strikes as heavy fighting and infrastructure destruction escalate

claims.text: US President Donald Trump stated that 25,000 people died in the Russia-Ukraine war last month, following 32,000 deaths the previous month and 33,000 two months prior.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged partners to respond strongly, stating on Saturday that Russia is escalating every single day.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated at the UN General Assembly that Russia is using nationals from 47 countries on the battlefield through deception and tricks.
A Ukrainian drone attack in Russia's southern Krasnodar region killed three people and damaged the Ilsky oil refinery.
A wave of Russian strikes hit various regions across Ukraine.
Russian and Ukrainian strikes killed at least 16 people over 24 hours across both countries and occupied territories.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukrainian air defences are intercepting 55 percent of jet-powered drones launched by Russia.
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov vowed that the objectives of Moscow's military operation in Ukraine will be achieved.
Russian strikes on Kyiv killed seven people and forced a halt to production at ArcelorMittal, Ukraine's largest steelmaker.
Russia's Defence Ministry stated that Russian forces struck a cargo vessel carrying military supplies near Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Washington proposed a meeting of Russian, Ukrainian, and US officials in the United Arab Emirates.
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov accused Europe at the UN General Assembly of doing everything it can to thwart peace talks supported by the Trump administration.

clusters.headline_hint: Pakistani Taliban suicide attack kills 12 near police post in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa

claims.text: A Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan suicide bomber rammed an explosives-laden tractor-trolley into the Aman Mela police checkpost in Dera Ismail Khan district.
At least 11 to 12 people were killed in the suicide attack on a police post in Dera Ismail Khan district.
Two customs and excise officials were among those killed in the Dera Ismail Khan bombing.
The suicide bombing occurred two days after border clashes between Pakistan and Afghanistan killed at least 13 Afghan Taliban fighters.
China, Turkey, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia are participating in mediation efforts to secure peace between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
The Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan ended its ceasefire with the Pakistani government in November 2022.
Around 30 people, mostly security personnel and passersby, were injured in the suicide blast at the Dera Ismail Khan checkpoint.
The Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan claimed responsibility for the suicide bombing in a statement.
Pakistan has repeatedly accused Kabul of allowing Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan members to operate from Afghan soil, an accusation Afghan authorities deny.

clusters.headline_hint: Hundreds of thousands assemble in central Paris as Pope Leo XIV holds massive open-air Mass

claims.text: Pope Leo XIV celebrated an outdoor Mass along the Avenue des Champs-Elysees in Paris with an estimated 800,000 people in attendance.
Brigitte Macron, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, far-right leader Marine Le Pen, and LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault attended Pope Leo XIV's Mass in Paris.
Pope Leo XIV's four-day trip to France marks the first official papal visit to the country in nearly two decades.
French President Emmanuel Macron did not attend the Mass in Paris, represented instead by his wife Brigitte.
A 2021 inquiry found that clergy or lay members of the Catholic Church in France abused about 330,000 people as minors over seven decades.
Pope Leo XIV visited the Maison Bakhita center in Paris, meeting with migrants and volunteers supporting refugees.
Pope Leo XIV cautioned against "losing our humanity amid a paradise of machines" regarding artificial intelligence during his visit to France.
Born Robert Prevost in Chicago in 1955, Pope Leo XIV is the first US-born pontiff.
A report by French statistics agency INSEE showed that only 25% of French 18-to-49-year-olds identified as Catholic, compared with 43% a decade earlier.
The Vatican estimated that 700,000 people turned out for Pope Leo XIV's outdoor Mass at Place de la Concorde in Paris.
About 14,500 police officers, gendarmes, military personnel, and firefighters were deployed to secure the papal event in Paris.

clusters.headline_hint: Election Commission issues clarifications and alters revision rules amidst intense national row and Opposition opposition

claims.text: Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray announced a joint public march with Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray in Mumbai on October 4, 2026, to protest the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
Raj Thackeray called the Election Commission of India a wing of the BJP and accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of committing fraud under the SIR process.
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu stated that the Election Commission's clarification reaffirmed the integrity and credibility of India's constitutional institutions.
LJP (Ram Vilas) chief Chirag Paswan questioned why opposition parties remain silent about electoral processes in states where they have formed governments.

Former Kerala Chief Secretary Jiji Thomson alleged that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar asked him on a flight in 2016 whether he was interested in contesting the 2019 Lok Sabha election as a BJP candidate.
Gyanesh Kumar became the 26th Chief Election Commissioner of India in February 2025.

The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised objections on record at least 14 times over a 10-month period concerning decisions made regarding the Special Intensive Revision without their knowledge.

The Election Commission stated on Saturday that decisions concerning the Special Intensive Revision had received unanimous approval from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.
The Election Commission announced that a committee including an independent expert from an IIT or IIIT will review ECINET.
The Election Commission announced measures including doorstep collection of documents from voters who have been issued notices during the Special Intensive Revision.
Cockroach Janta Party leader Abhijeet Dipke called for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation following allegations that Kumar offered a BJP election ticket in 2016.

The Cockroach Janta Party launched its 'Election Commission Thik Karo' campaign, citing the exclusion of more than 13 crore names from draft electoral rolls across 30 states and Union Territories during the Special Intensive Revision.
Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray backed calls for protests in Mumbai against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar beginning October 2.

clusters.headline_hint: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar addresses UNGA, heavily criticizing Pakistan over state-sponsored terrorism

claims.text: Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar described Pakistan as a 'serial practitioner of terrorism' during his address at the 81st United Nations General Assembly.
Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif credited US President Donald Trump for intervening to end the India-Pakistan military conflict last year.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar reiterated India's support for a two-state solution to achieve durable peace in the Israel-Palestine conflict.
Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called Kashmir Pakistan's 'jugular vein' and accused India of human rights violations during his speech at the UN General Assembly.
Eighteen Indians have been among the seafarers killed during attacks linked to conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia.
India joined Liberia and 23 other partner nations in a global initiative to oppose attacks on commercial shipping in international waterways.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi skipped the UN General Assembly session in 2026, marking the fifth time External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar delivered India's National Statement.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar called for targeting and exposing the financial networks that sustain terrorism.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar noted during his UNGA address that the war in Ukraine was nearing its fifth year.
US President Donald Trump reshared an 87-second video clip of Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's UNGA speech on Truth Social without adding comment.
India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7 last year against terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir following an attack in Pahalgam on April 22 that killed 26 civilians.
India rejected claims of US mediation, asserting that Operation Sindoor was paused after a request from Pakistan's Director General of Military Operations.

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar cited Prime Minister Narendra Modi's earlier remarks highlighting how regional conflicts in West Asia disrupt global energy security, maritime trade, and supply chains.
